---
applyTo: "spec/actions/**/*.rb"
---

# Action specs

- Write action specs as unit specs. Stub everything the action calls, and check that it calls each one with the right arguments, e.g. `post = instance_double(Post)` then `expect(post).to receive(:update!).with(archived_at: Time.zone.now)` before `described_class.call(post)`. Avoid creating records in action specs, even when the action runs a query.
- In action specs, name the `describe` block after the method the spec calls, e.g. `describe ".call"`.
- If an action spec needs a lot of stubs to set up, split the action into smaller actions.
- In action specs, check the action's `Error` by stubbing a collaborator to raise the original error, e.g. `allow(post).to receive(:update!).and_raise(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid)` then `expect { described_class.call(post) }.to raise_error(described_class::Error)`.
- In action specs, stub other actions the action calls too, e.g. `expect(Posts::UnpublishPost).to receive(:call).with(post)` in the spec for `Posts::ArchivePost`. To check the action wraps the other action's error, stub the other action to raise it, e.g. `allow(Posts::UnpublishPost).to receive(:call).and_raise(Posts::UnpublishPost::Error)`.
- When an action writes to a relation, stub the method that returns it to return an `instance_double(ActiveRecord::Relation)` and expect the write, e.g. `allow(Comment).to receive(:on_posts).with(posts).and_return(comments)` then `expect(comments).to receive(:update_all).with(locked: true, updated_at: Time.zone.now)`. Pass a relation double in as the records, e.g. `posts = instance_double(ActiveRecord::Relation)`.
- When an action loops with `find_each`, stub it to yield doubles, e.g. `allow(posts).to receive(:find_each).and_yield(post)`.
- When an action takes a lock, stub `with_lock` to yield, e.g. `allow(post).to receive(:with_lock).and_yield`. To test the check inside the lock, return one answer for the check before the lock and another for the check inside it, e.g. `allow(post).to receive(:published?).and_return(false, true)`.
- When an action enqueues a job, stub the job's class method and check its arguments, e.g. `expect(PublishScheduledPostJob).to receive(:perform_later_for).with(post)` in the spec for `Posts::EnqueuePublishes`.
- When an action works out a job's arguments, stub the values it reads them from to cover each case, and check the arguments it passes, e.g. `instance_double(Post, newsletter_id?: true, newsletter_id: "newsletter-1")` then `expect(RefreshNewsletterStatsJob).to receive(:perform_later).with("newsletter-1")`, and `newsletter_id?: false` with `expect(RefreshNewsletterStatsJob).not_to receive(:perform_later)`.
- In action specs, stub another service like any other collaborator, with an `instance_double` returned from the method the action builds it with, e.g. `instance_double(NewsletterClient)` returned from `NewsletterClient.new`. You MUST NOT stub the HTTP request in an action spec.
- In action specs, when the action builds the service with its default constructor, build the stubbed client in a `let` and stub the constructor in a `before`, e.g. `let(:newsletter_client) { instance_double(NewsletterClient) }` with `before { allow(NewsletterClient).to receive(:new).and_return(newsletter_client) }`. You SHOULD stub the client's methods in each example, e.g. `allow(newsletter_client).to receive(:create_newsletter).with(post)`. When every example in a `context` needs the same stub, you MAY stub it in a `before` in that context instead, e.g. in `context "when the newsletter service fails"`.
- In action specs, when the action builds the service for a record, e.g. `NewsletterClient.for(integration)`, write a helper method that takes the record and returns the stubbed client, instead of a `let`. Name it `stub_<service>_for`, e.g. `stub_newsletter_client_for(integration)`, and define it at the bottom of the spec file, inside the top-level `describe` block, after the examples.
- In action specs, check the action's errors by stubbing the service to raise an error built with the details a real failure carries, not the bare class, e.g. `allow(newsletter_client).to receive(:create_newsletter).with(post).and_raise(NewsletterClient::Error.new("Server error", status: 500))` then `expect { described_class.call(post) }.to raise_error(described_class::ServiceError)`.
- In action specs, stub each method that the action's argument validations call on a record double, e.g. `instance_double(Post, has_changes_to_save?: false)` for `unmodified:`.
